item.content:encoded:
I feel the execution actually lacks a deeper dive into this concept. It is too short for what it should be. Not saying that a skip must be long, but that this particular skip had left too many blank details that hit me as lazy research more than mystery.

Questions I want answers for
Even if the answer is just a greater mystery

1- How do you answer to the ad? Is it a standard telephone number? An address to send a letter? A directed intention?

2- What features can be made from the interview and the interviewer? Where on the building does the interview dream starts? What are the patterns, and what are not? How they even know that the building is entirely windowless? Even "dream knowledge" is a valid answer, but none was given. And If the dream is so vivid, "dream knowledge" will be the least adequate answer.

3- How is work at Pellus? I mean, buildings, companies and workplaces aren't uniformly equal across the globe. Are there closed cubicles or several people sharing the same work area? How much freedom do they have to talk among themselves, or to do any other activity? Even the dullest workplace have something more to it than just having windows or not, and it doesn't even seems particularly dull.

4- What could be found during an exploration of the building? The Foundation certainly wouldn't refrain from instructing someone to find out as much as possible about the place. It would be interesting to at least reference explorations for the building, the world where "fired" people dream, and the "payment" dreams. It would be fitting for those explorations to be at least mentioned to have happened.

In short, I see a lot of potential, and a very interesting concept, but too much focus on making the basic concept clear and very little elaboration on it.

Heh, I had a dream last night about interviewing for some weird-ass company, so I idly checked SCP-Wiki to see if a similar thing existed, and lo and behold… ;)

Relevant entry from Xaserdreamlog:

"Apparently, last night I interviewed with a California tech start-up company that I'm pretty sure was also a cult. I was flown down for 2 or 3 days for a multi-interview session which for some reason included church-youth-group-ish round table discussions about tech topics (i lied and told them my name was 'Xavier Acheron' in real life). Also the office building was formerly a military bunker and all employees slept there for some reason (i also stayed there on the first night); at some point during the night some guy took an unflattering photo of the CEO wearing pajamas (he looked like a stereotypical hipster) and everybody was terrified of that fact for some reason. Also, everybody was constantly repping the burritos cooked in the office (such that their recruitment literature repeatedly mentioned the burritos), with one guy stating that eating them will 'make you never want to leave.' I'm glad I didn't find out whether or not my dream-self took the position."

[…I suppose now that I think about it, I never did experience the second night in the dream, which according to the article means I've still got the technical interview coming up. Buggernuts.]

It would not improve the article. For me, the best part of this is the implied rat race trap. It's not malevolent. They aren't out to get you. They make you an offer that you are free to refuse and if you accept they make good on their end of the deal and nothing more. And then you have to abide by your side of the deal or else.

I usually really hate corporate metaphors, because they are usually written by people who are lazy both intellectually and physically. But this one strikes the perfect tone. It's neither heavy handed or unrealistic.
